name: No-white-cast daily SPF

card.summary: A sunscreen that sinks in without a pale or ashy film so it can be worn every day, helping protect skin from sun-related ageing and uneven tone.
card.note: Protection depends on applying enough product and reapplying.

quick.overview:
A no-white-cast daily SPF is a sunscreen formulated or tinted so it leaves no visible pale layer on the skin. Because skin ageing and uneven tone are driven in part by sun exposure, a product people will actually wear daily supports a more even, youthful-looking complexion over time.

White cast is most associated with mineral filters such as zinc oxide and titanium dioxide, whose larger particles can leave an opaque film; adding iron oxide pigments or using chemical filters changes how a product looks.
quick.how: People work a broad-spectrum sunscreen into the morning skincare routine as the last step before makeup or going out, choosing a tinted, sheer or fluid formula that suits their skin tone. Label guidance in general is to reapply roughly every two hours of sun exposure.
quick.risks: Some filters have been restricted in certain places for environmental reasons, and some aerosol products have been found contaminated with benzene. Most people apply less than the tested amount, which lowers real-world protection.

lead: A no-white-cast daily SPF is a sunscreen that blends invisibly into skin, so that wearing it every day does not mean a visible pale film. Mineral sunscreens with larger particles often leave an opaque white cast that consumers find unacceptable, while tints with iron oxide pigments can also add protection against visible light [1].

The appearance case is photoageing: a 2013 Australian study of about 900 light-skinned adults, as summarised on Wikipedia, found that those told to apply broad-spectrum sunscreen every day for four and a half years had smoother, more resilient skin than controls [1].

chain: Worn daily under or without makeup
Less UV-driven ageing and uneven tone
Skin looks smoother and more even
angle.text: Cosmetic appeal is what makes daily use realistic: a formula that doesn't leave a pale film is easier to wear on all skin tones every day.

infobox: Mineral (zinc oxide, titanium dioxide) or organic [1]
Tints, iron oxide, smaller particles, organic filters [1]

paras: Mineral filters work mainly by absorbing UV with some reflection and scattering; larger-particle versions can give broader protection but often leave an opaque white film [1]. US labels need not disclose nanoparticle ingredients, while EU labels must [1].

SPF measures protection against sunburn-producing UVB; it does not measure UVA, so broad-spectrum labelling matters [1]. Most people apply about a quarter to a half of the tested amount, which reduces effective SPF [1].

The Australian trial of about 900 adults and a 32-subject study of daily SPF 30 over 12 weeks to one year are summarised on Wikipedia [1]. No studies specific to white-cast-free formulas as a category were found.

timeline.event: Franz Greiter introduces the sun protection factor [1].
Zinc oxide approved as a UV filter in the EU [1].
